newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela and Mexico offer extra crude to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Venezuela and Mexico offer extra crude to U.S..

text.p: U.S. refiners have been offered extra barrels of Venezuelan and Mexican crude as recently as last week, but demand remains lukewarm, traders said Tuesday.

Seasonally thin demand for heavy grades, with the passing of the summer asphalt season, and the approval of further sales of sour crude from the government's Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), have combined to suppress demand.

"We are not term buyers but they called us last week," a U.S. East Coast trader said, referring to calls from a unit of Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) for spot barrels, adding that term customers are typically approached first.
Venezuela was seen offering additional barrels of Furrial and Mesa crude oil, heavy sour grades, traders said.
Mexico's state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (PEMEX) has also sounded out term customers for extra supply.
"The Mexicans are offering crude on a 'when-do-you-want-it basis,'" a Midwest refiner said, noting a flexibility with volumes and timing.
Term customers said Mexico could provide Maya, Olmeca and Isthmus crudes, but did not cite significant discounts.
When contacted, a PEMEX source said he was not aware of additional barrels being offered to the market.
"Sellers are trying to be discreet. The Mexican's have either lost market share to Venezuela, or their production has increased," the East Coast trader said.
Venezuela is widely believed to be producing more than 3.0 million barrels per day (bpd), way above its OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd.
Mexico's crude production is about 2.85 million bpd, with exports seen around 1.5 million bpd. About one million barrels is exported to the U.S.
